When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out: the new Siri Recap and a significantly improved heart rate monitor. While these were part of why I picked up the new Apple Watch, I discovered there was much more to get excited about.

Battery and Charging

Although Apple's website does not list any extra battery life improvement for the Apple Watch Series 12 over the Series 11, battery life does feel longer. As I wrote in the past, before using the Apple Watch Series 12, I was a WHOOP user, and although I kept my Apple Watch around, I never used it for sleep tracking.

After the event, I decided to give Apple Watch sleep tracking a try. That said, on my Series 11, it was a bit of a juggling act to track sleep and charge simultaneously. After wearing the watch all day, I had to give it a brief charge before bed, then another when I woke up in the morning.

The Series 12 doesn't have this problem. It has enough juice to get through the day and overnight, and now I just charge it when I wake up. The Apple Watch Series 12 also charges significantly faster, making charging far less of a hassle. According to Apple, just 15 minutes of charging delivers up to 12 hours of battery life.

I suspect the brand-new S11 chip (derived from the 2nm design of the A20 Pro) is a major reason battery life feels so much longer. Regardless of the reason, not having to stress about charging for sleep tracking on the Apple Watch Series 12 is a delight. Another big advantage of the S11 chip is that the Apple Watch Series 12 is significantly faster, especially when it comes to Siri.

Exclusive Software Features

The Series 12 finally introduces an official step counter as a watch face complication, which I like seeing in the Smart Stack. Will this feature trickle down to older Apple Watches? Quite possibly. After all, Apple wasn't not counting steps before—it just counts them more accurately on the Apple Watch Series 12, but since the data already exists, I'd argue Apple should just add the complication. Regardless, it's nice to have it on the Series 12.

Another fun new addition is the brand-new Readiness app, which tells you how you're doing today based on your sleep last night, your activity the day before, and your vitals. This is similar to the recovery score on WHOOP, and I'm thrilled Apple has added this to the Apple Watch. It's a bit unfortunate this is exclusive to the Series 12, but I can understand Apple not wanting to calculate this metric with less accurate data.

The Wrap Up

All in all, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a pretty nice upgrade. This is very much an 'S' year upgrade, but if you care about whether the Apple Watch can actually do more—and not just look different—I'd say this is the most meaningful year-over-year upgrade since the Apple Watch Series 4.

Compared to the Series 10 and 11, the case is ever-so-slightly thicker. As someone who uses black watch faces, I can't say I really noticed this—but I'd like to see Apple improve this next generation.

One last thing worth mentioning: the Apple Watch Series 12 brings Ceramic Shield 2 to the aluminum models, making it far more scratch-resistant than older Apple Watch models. I've only owned this watch for a short time, so I haven't truly put this to the test, but so far, my Apple Watch looks as good as new.
